summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and the gate blocked the run (simulation_allowed=false, comparison_valid=false). Studio did not run: simulation status is 'skipped' because the custom experiment has no floorplan blocks and no power_w object, so there is no Studio output. The scenario is WaFFLe (gated LLC ways plus per-core fine-grained DVFS) on a 16-core tiled CMP with an 8MB LLC. The paper reports a peak temperature reduction of 8.4 C, an average temperature reduction of 6.2 C and 2.5% IPS degradation versus baseline, with GDP1 at 6.1 C and GDP2 at 6.7 C peak reduction. These are maximum reductions over nine PARSEC applications from a coupled gem5/McPAT/HotSpot transient simulation at 0.33 us intervals. The experiment was labeled custom_2d_steady, which has no transient trace, and cannot represent a runtime controller whose gains come from time-varying power. No numerical comparison with Studio is made or valid, since the location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions do not match and no Studio result exists. Qualitatively, lowering power in cores and cache banks should lower temperature, but that is a general expectation and not a replication or validation of the 8.4 C figure. The final verdict is that the paper is not reproducible in Studio from the packet. The independent page/asset review and the adversarial checks are also unresolved, so none of the extracted evidence is independently verified.
limitations: Studio did not run, so no simulated temperatures exist and no quantitative comparison with the 8.4 C, 6.2 C or 2.5% figures is valid.
The experiment is custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and empty power_w, so it fails input validation (1–128 blocks plus power_w required).
The paper's observable is a maximum reduction versus baseline across nine PARSEC applications from transient simulation; a static steady-state map would differ in regime and aggregation.
The packet publishes no block-level geometry (x, y, width, height), no per-block power table, and no die, TIM, heat spreader, heat sink or material parameters.
Power comes from a coupled gem5/McPAT run with temperature-dependent leakage feedback. This runtime behavior and the per-application power traces are not available to Studio.
The DVFS reaction (about 70 ns) and the 2M-cycle way-gating interval cannot be represented by fixed block powers.
The LLC size is ambiguous: Table 1 lists 1MB 16-way L2 per tile (16MB total) while Table 3 uses 8MB.
Cooling and package details are unspecified, so a cooling-boundary mismatch with Studio cannot be excluded; the 47 C ambient is the only boundary value published.
Evidence entries failed locator validation, and the adversarial code, parameter, config and data checks are unresolved, so the extraction is unverified.
No linked assets or repositories were found, and figure digitization would give only qualitative layouts without dimensional scale.
No exact replication is claimed; the verdict is gated as not 2D applicable.
